message.content: how does login work in this app? explain with a diagram

content.text:
Short version: login is a three-hop handshake. The browser sends credentials, the API checks them against the database, and you get back a short-lived access token plus a refresh token.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant B as Browser
    participant A as Auth API
    participant D as Database
    B->>A: POST /login
    A->>D: find user, compare hash
    D-->>A: user record
    A-->>B: access + refresh tokens
    B->>A: GET /me with access token
    A-->>B: profile
```

Here's the walkthrough. The browser posts the email and password to `src/auth/login.ts`. The API looks the user up and compares the password against the stored bcrypt hash, so the raw password never touches the database. If it matches, `issueTokens()` signs a fifteen-minute access token and a two-week refresh token.

## What happens when the token expires

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    R[Request] --> V{Access token valid?}
    V -- yes --> OK[Serve request]
    V -- no --> F{Refresh token valid?}
    F -- yes --> N[Issue new pair] --> OK
    F -- no --> L[Back to login]
```

Every request first checks the access token. When it has expired, the client quietly trades its refresh token for a fresh pair, so the user never notices. Only when the refresh token is also gone do we send them back to the login screen.

```ts
const { access, refresh } = await issueTokens(user.id)
```

If you want, I can add refresh-token rotation next, so a stolen refresh token only works once.
